messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Recommended data structure for censored data
parts:
This one also never got answered.

IWhat is I[i, t] and why are you defining alpha
as something that looks like a mixture?

I don't know what f(.) smoothing means.

What you wan tto do is treat this like a mixture model
or latent-discrete parameter model (separate chapters in
the manual) and marginalize I[i, t] out. That should
be tractable because the likelihood isolates the I[i, t]
with data items y[i, t].

- Bob

> On Jul 26, 2016, at 8:36 PM, SB Lee <sblee...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi, I'm rather new to stan and now trying to build a hierarchical model using stan.
> The model in my mind is
> Given y_it, N_it,
> y_it ~ binomial_logit(N_it, p_it)
> logit(p_it) = alpha + beta*X1_it + f(X2_it)
> alpha = alpha_1 (1 - I_it) + alpha_2 I_it
> X1, X2: predictors, f(.): smoothing
> I_it ~ binary outcome with some random process in mind
>
> So the model itself is binomial logit regression with varying slope and intercept, and intercept modeled with mixture.
> Now the problem is that my data are like patient specimen which means for each subject i, y_it and N_it are available only for different certain time range t. (For example, for y_1t available for t=1~5, y_2t available for t=2~4, and so on.) I first thought of assigning 0 to both N_it and y_it for missing cases, but that certainly is not the wise way to do so. Also, it seems that STAN does not support discrete index mixing so that accessing data within STAN for my case is rather confusing. (I looked at reference page about censored data but it doesn't seem to fit in my case.) Are there any suggestion for data structure to start with, please?
>
